USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Proceed with the proposed List 3 tariffs on ~$200B of Chinese goods at 25%, while signaling willingness to negotiate if China offers structural concessions on IP theft, forced tech transfer, and industrial subsidies. The tariffs serve as both leverage and a genuine corrective measure; backing down now would squander momentum and embolden Beijing.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat score of +0.35 reflects moderate but real damage. On the positive side, US industrial production is growing (104.03 in Aug, up 1.8% over the window), the dollar has strengthened ~7% (115.15 index), and the economy absorbed List 1 tariffs without visible macro damage. However, consumer sentiment has declined from 101.4 to 96.2 (-5.1%), soybean prices collapsed ~25% forcing USDA to announce $12B in emergency farmer aid (July 24), and business groups warn of $1.3T in potential costs if the war fully escalates (RSM estimate). The agricultural sector is already in genuine distress from China's retaliatory tariffs on soybeans and pork.

The action score of -0.4 (moderate escalation) is justified by three factors: (1) The Section 301 findings document real, structural Chinese IP theft and forced tech transfer that harms US long-term competitiveness — this is not a manufactured dispute. (2) China cannot fully retaliate in kind due to the ~$375B trade deficit gap, giving the US asymmetric leverage. (3) Chinese yuan has depreciated ~6% (from 6.28 to ~6.64 per dollar), partially offsetting tariff effects, suggesting China is already absorbing pain. However, escalation should be targeted and procedural (following the formal List 3 comment process already underway) rather than reckless, to maintain allied support and domestic political legitimacy. The risk of consumer price increases on furniture, appliances, and electronics from List 3 is real, but the structural IP/tech-transfer issues justify bearing that cost now rather than accepting permanent disadvantage.

Chinese yuan depreciated ~6% (6.28 → 6.64/USD), partially offsetting tariff effects

sources_cited.excerpt: At Trump's direction, USTR says it is considering raising the proposed List 3 rate from 10% to 25%
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines)
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
Consumer sentiment declined from 101.4 (Mar) to 96.2 (Aug), a 5.1% drop
Industrial production rose from 102.2 (Mar) to 104.0 (Aug), up 1.8%
Broad dollar index rose from 107.6 (Feb) to 115.2 (Aug), up 7.0%
USDA will authorize up to $12 billion in programs, which is in line with the estimated $11 billion impact of the unjustified retaliatory tariffs on U.S. agricultural goods
If the tariff policy is fully implemented, the costs will likely exceed $1.3 trillion with the risk of a much greater hit to the U.S. economy
From early April, when the talk of trade wars began in earnest and the Chinese yuan was valued at 6.28 to the dollar, the currency has depreciated by 6 percent to 6.64 to the dollar as of July 6
